newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end mixed, local bonds gain.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end mixed, local bonds gain.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished mixed Wednesday with local instruments holding up on the back of a rumor that the country is going to issue a five-year bond denominated in pesos.
"There was a rumor of a five-year peso bond and that helped the market, above all local instruments," said a trader at a foreign bank.

Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was down 1/8 at 93-7/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was down $0.02 at 121.09. The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 rose $0.20 to 117.80.
Otherwise, the market was held back by a rise in the U.S. 30-year yield. It was last last up four basis points at 6.74 percent.
"In general the market weathered the rise in U.S. yields well," said another trader. "There was little genuine trade," he added.
Above all, the market was eagerly awaiting word on U.S. interest rates, when the Federal Open Market Committee meets next week, for direction.
In money markets, call money was stable at 5.70 percent.
